title: Japan's Egg Prices at Record Highs
paragraphs: Eggs used to be something people in Japan could buy without worrying about the price.
But that's changing. Egg prices are now at record highs — and they could go even higher.

In September, the average price of 10 eggs was 309 yen, or about $2. That's the highest price ever recorded in Japan — although it was just as high in May and June, before going down a little in July and August.
Why are eggs getting so expensive?
One reason is the increasing cost of chicken feed. Japan buys much of its chicken feed from other countries, and prices have gone up because of the conflict in the Middle East and the weaker yen.
But there's another worry — bird flu, which can kill chickens, could make the situation worse.
Japan has had bird flu outbreaks every year since 2020.

During the 2022-23 bird flu season, 18 million birds were killed to stop the flu from spreading. This meant there weren't enough eggs, and some businesses, including McDonald's Japan, had to stop selling certain foods made with eggs.
Now, egg farmers and food companies are looking for ways to prevent another egg shortage.
Some companies are buying eggs from other countries. For example, Japanese food company Kewpie has been buying eggs from Brazil since 2023.
Others are looking at using more frozen eggs, which can be kept for longer.
The government is also thinking about using vaccines to help keep chickens safe from bird flu.
With the busy Christmas season coming soon, Japan is hoping to stop egg prices from going even higher.
